proposal:
Here is the canonicalized PostgreSQL `SELECT` statement:

```sql
SELECT
    t1.encodetype AS encoding_method,
    COUNT(*) AS occurrence_count,
    AVG(t3.complexidx) AS avg_complexity_measure,
    AVG(t2.snrratio) AS avg_quality_ratio,
    t2.signalregistry AS signal_registry,
    t2.timemark AS signal_timestamp
FROM
    signaldecoding AS t1
JOIN
    signals AS t2 ON t1.signalref = t2.signalregistry
JOIN
    signalclassification AS t3 ON t2.signalregistry = t3.signalref
GROUP BY
    t1.encodetype, t2.signalregistry, t2.timemark
ORDER BY
    occurrence_count DESC;
```

This query is already well-formatted and follows PostgreSQL conventions, so no changes were necessary. The columns, aliases, ordering, and grouping are preserved as requested.
